events.title: Using Glycobiology to Improve Cancer Immunotherapeutics with Charles J. Dimitroff, Ph.D.
events.description: Charles J. Dimitroff, Ph.D., is a professor at FIU Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine (FIU Medicine) and a translational glycobiology researcher. His research focuses on how complex sugars, known as glycans, regulate immune and cancer cell functions, with the goal of developing new approaches to strengthen the immune system, combat disease and slow cancer progression. The Dimitroff Lab at FIU Medicine uses advanced technologies and model systems, including carbohydrate inhibitors, MALDI-TOF-TOF MS/MS, selectin and galectin chimeras, glycosyltransferase mutant models and human tissue samples, to study inflammation, cancer development and metastasis, tumor immune evasion, lymphoma development and other mechanisms of disease. REGISTER HERE Lunch will be provided. This event is part of the Department of Cellular & Molecular Medicine Seminar Series.

events.title: Managing Cash Flow Through Opportunities and Challenges
events.description: Is your business having a difficult time managing your cash flow? Given economic uncertainties and price/labor cost increases, managing your company’s cash flow is more important than ever. This allows you to cover expenses, take advantage of strategic opportunities, and meet your goals for the business. This webinar will help business owners will better understand the vital role cash flow plays in the success of a business. Managing the timing of when money enters and exits a company is crucial to the survival of the business and to its ability to fund future growth. After attending this webinar, business owners will be able to better control the availability of cash in their business.

events.title: EmpowerED: Your Future Self Will Thank You for Showing Up on Sept 23
events.description: Hey BizPanthers! A full afternoon isn’t required. A plan is. EmpowerED is a come-and-go student resource event designed to help FIU Business students make the most of their college experience and prepare for what comes next. Stop by anytime between noon and 5 p.m. to meet student organizations, connect with Career Services, explore scholarships and study abroad opportunities, get a professional headshot, and enjoy food, refreshments, and giveaways. Students are especially encouraged to plan their visit around two conversations with FIU Business alumni: 🕛 12:45–1:35 p.m. | Vania Arredondo (BBA ’23), founder of FOMI - “Things I Wish I Knew When I Was a Student” 🕒 3:15–4:05 p.m. | Daniel Marin (MBA ’11, BS ’05), executive director of public relations for FIFA World Cup 2026 Come for one session or build your afternoon around both. Resources and activities will be available throughout the event. 🤝 Connect with FIU Business leadership, get answers to your questions, and gain insights to help you succeed. 📅 Register today and save your spot! Don’t just survive college—get EmpowerED.

events.title: Latin America and Caribbean Book Series: An Evening with Dr.Ivelaw Griffith
events.description: FIU's Latin American and Caribbean Center and Books & Books proudly present an evening with Dr. Ivelaw L. Griffith at Books & Books. Book Description: Guyana resides in an oil- endowed neighborhood, along with Venezuela, Brazil, Colombia, and Trinidad and Tobago as major oil and gas producers and Suriname rising in the petro production ranks. However, South America’s sole Anglophone republic is also located in a wet neighborhood, where climate change has begun to impact society and can diminish some of the oil gains. This dual reality requires understanding the vicissitudes of the promise of oil and the potential peril of climate change. This book undertakes this task. It examines the dynamics of the country’s oil pursuits in the context of its political environment, assesses its physical and social geography and its environmental security vulnerability that has been accentuated by climate change factors, and explains the geoeconomic and geopolitical implications of Venezuela’s claim to Essequibo for the country’s petro power pursuits. The book also carries an appendix with fun facts about the country’s oil, gas, and climate change realities. Dr. Ivelaw Griffith is a Fellow with the Caribbean Policy Consortium and a former Senior Associate with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has published widely on Caribbean affairs.

events.title: Mental Health, Innovation, Normalization and Destigmatization Symposium
events.description: The Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Health at FIU Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine are pleased to host the inaugural Mental Health, Innovation, Normalization, and Destigmatization Symposium (MINDS). LEARN MORE AND REGISTER HERE This community-centered symposium will bring together individuals with lived experience, mental health advocates, community partners, academic leaders and psychiatrists to foster meaningful conversations and action on mental health. We are entering a transformative era in mental health care defined by integrated, person-centered approaches that acknowledge the biological, psychological, social and cultural factors that shape well-being. Emerging research and practice are expanding traditional models to include holistic, community-based and culturally responsive strategies that promote early intervention, resilience and cross-sector collaboration. MINDS offers a platform for these innovations by addressing stigma, encouraging open dialogue and strengthening community partnerships.

events.title: BSI Seminar Social Title: “Will AI Save Us or Kill Us?”
events.description: Title: “Will AI Save Us or Kill Us?” By: Prem Chapagain, Ph.D. Professor, Department of Physics Associate Director, Biomolecular Sciences Institute Florida International University Abstract: For centuries, physics has sought to understand nature through fundamental laws and predictive models. Today, we are applying this same predictive philosophy to the extraordinary complexity of biology. Advances in molecular dynamics, machine learning, and AI are transforming our ability to predict biomolecular structures, dynamics, interactions, and ultimately design new therapeutics. From emerging pandemics to antibiotic resistance and cancer, AI offers the possibility of dramatically accelerating the discovery of medicines and solutions to global health challenges. Yet the rapid emergence of increasingly capable and autonomous AI systems also raises profound questions about safety and control. This talk explores the remarkable journey from physics to molecular simulation to AI-driven biology, and asks a fundamental question: will AI become one of our greatest tools for solving humanity’s challenges, or one of our greatest risks? Short Bio: Dr. Prem Chapagain is a Professor of Physics at Florida International University and Associate Director of the Biomolecular Sciences Institute. His research applies principles of physics, molecular dynamics, structural biology, and artificial intelligence to understand how biomolecules move, interact, and function. His group uses computational and machine-learning approaches to address questions in biology and drug discovery, with applications to human health. He is particularly interested in harnessing emerging AI technologies to accelerate our ability to understand and design biological systems. The seminar will take place in person on Friday, September 25th, 2026, from 11:30 AM to 1:00 PM in ZEB 150, MMC Campus. Light refreshments and snacks will be provided from 11:30 AM to noon, followed by the Seminar at 12:00 PM. Students, please bring your OneCard.

events.description: Caring for someone you love can be deeply meaningful, but it can also bring emotional, physical, and personal challenges that are difficult to carry alone. The Caring & Sharing Support Group offers a safe and nurturing space for caregivers to connect with others who understand the caregiving journey. It is a place to feel heard, understood, supported, and cared for** while sharing experiences, gaining perspective, and drawing strength from one another. Together, we create space not only to care for those we love, but also to remember the importance of caring for ourselves along the way. The support group meets the last Friday at every month at 12 noon via Zoom Come as you are. Connect, share, and be supported.

events.title: Beyond Nietzsche: The Music of Peter Gast
events.description: Peter Gast (1854–1918), composer, editor, and collaborator of Friedrich Nietzsche, played a significant role in the publication of Nietzsche’s writings. This evening of live performance and conversation examines Gast’s career, his relationship with Nietzsche, and his work as a composer. The program features FIU Associate Professor of Voice Robert B. Dundas, The Wolfsonian’s Chief Librarian Frank Luca, soprano Hannah Gauthier, and pianist Juvenal Correa-Salas. Presented in partnership with the Consulate General of the Federal Republic of Germany and the FIU Wertheim School of Music & the Performing Arts.

events.title: Professional Science Master's in Environmental Policy and Management Seminar
events.description: Title: How journalism can move audiences from awareness to action through community-centered storytelling by Dr. Yulia Strokova, founder and publisher of Impact.Edition Abstract Featured Discussion How can journalism move people from awareness to action? Drawing on her experience as the founder and publisher of Impact.Edition, Dr. Yulia Strokova will explore how solutions-focused journalism can spotlight credible responses to social and environmental challenges while remaining rigorous, critical, and independent. Through Miami-based examples, she will discuss how journalists can center community voices, examine evidence of impact, and avoid simplistic “hero narratives.” She will also demonstrate how stories can extend beyond the page through public exhibitions, print publications, newsletters, events, and partnerships, reaching new audiences and creating opportunities for participation. The presentation invites emerging journalists to think beyond documenting problems and consider how thoughtful, community-centered storytelling can inspire community engagement and drive meaningful action.

events.title: THE ADAPTIVE HOME: A Book Talk with Professor Sam Moshaver.
events.description: You are invited to hear Dr. Sam Moshaver talk about his new book: The Adaptive Home: Supplementary Space Design for an Uncertain Future. The book provides a comprehensive guide for architects, urban planners, and developers on designing and retrofitting residential environments to meet the evolving needs of residents. About the Author Dr. Sam Moshaver is an Assistant Professor of Interior Architecture in the School of Architecture at Florida International University. He also serves as co-director of the Collaboratory for Design Environment & Cognition (CODEC) Lab, where his empirical research investigates environment-behavior studies, neuroinclusive design, and spatial comfort.

events.title: Tumor Glycans in Pancreatic Cancer Development, Progression and Immune Suppression with Susan L. Bellis, Ph.D.
events.description: Susan Bellis is a professor in the Department of Cell, Developmental and Integrative Biology at the University of Alabama at Birmingham. Research in the Bellis Laboratory focuses on the effects of glycosylation on the structure and function of cell surface receptors involved in cancer development, progression and immune suppression. She is a member of the Alliance of Glycobiologists for Cancer Research, sponsored by the National Cancer Institute. She recently received the Springer Nature Editor of Distinction Award. Bellis has played leadership roles in the glycoscience field, including as the 2023 President of the Society for Glycobiology. REGISTER HERE Lunch will be provided. This event is part of the Dr. Herbert and Nicole Wertheim Leadership Lecture Series.

events.title: NorthMed FIU: General Club Tabling
events.description: Stop by and meet NorthMed! NorthMed is dedicated to supporting pre-medical and pre-health students through community, mentorship, and practical clinical experience. Whether you are seeking advice on the pre-med pathway, looking to connect with like-minded peers, or interested in hands-on clinical opportunities, our executive board is here to help you get connected. Drop by our table to: Learn more about NorthMed’s mission and upcoming Fall semester initiatives. Get information on our clinical skills events, including our upcoming CPR & Basic Life Support (BLS) workshop and MCAT preparation sessions. Discover mentorship outreach and leadership development opportunities. Ask questions about prerequisite coursework, research, volunteering, and life as an FIU pre-health student. Join our Panther Connect roster and member communication channels. All FIU students interested in medicine, healthcare, and allied sciences are welcome to stop by! FUNDED BY SGA

events.description: Tuesday Times Roundtable TTR is FIU’s weekly series of moderated conversations around current global issues and trends. Conversations bring into play the multiple viewpoints of students, faculty, staff, and community members. All sessions are absolutely FREE and lunch is on us! TTR: The Unsung Ally: Spain and the Birth of the United States Presenters: Elsa Hoyo Jornet, Director of the Spanish Resource Center in Miami at FIU & Technical Advisor at the Education Office of Spain in Miami Rafael Serrano, Visiting Teacher, DDCUS (Doral Downtown Charter Upper School) Begoña Santos, Executive Director, Queen Sofia Spanish Institute SDG Topic Category: SDG4: Quality Education News Article: https://go.fiu.edu/ttr0929 Description: Inspired by the New York Times article “Sure, France Helped the Colonists. These initiatives encouraged students to reflect on the shared history between Spain and the United States and to recognize the lasting impact of Spanish figures, resources, and military efforts on the nation’s path to independence. events.title: Get Better Results:  Effective Content Engineering for AI
events.description: Are you providing the best context to your AI to get the results you are looking for? Business owners are now using AI more than ever before to start and grow their small businesses. However, many users are either overloading their AI or not using the right strategies to receive optimal results. Effective content engineering involves a blend of: · Improved Systems Instructions · Being Intentional and Concise With Examples · Optimizing Relevant Background Within AI Model Constraints After attending this webinar you will better understand content engineering and how to use a broader strategy to get the best results for your business.

events.description: Chào các em học sinh! Interested in studying abroad in Vietnam, Cambodia, and Thailand? Students have the opportunity to earn their Honors credits through the faculty-led study abroad program: Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia: 2,000 Years of History with Co-Faculty Directors Cory Fairfield and Eloisa Rodriguez-Dod. events.title: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ
events.description: La Hora del Café is a weekly conversation and community-building event hosted by the Department of Modern Languages at Florida International University (FIU). The event provides students, faculty, and language enthusiasts with an informal and welcoming environment to practice Spanish, strengthen intercultural communication skills, and connect with members of the FIU community. Held every Tuesday from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Department of Modern Languages (SIPA II, Room 216), La Hora del Café encourages participants of all proficiency levels to engage in spontaneous conversations in Spanish while enjoying complimentary coffee and pastries sponsored by Café Bustelo. The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty.

events.title: SHRM General Body Meeting
events.description: Join SHRM and build the confidence, skills, and professional presence you need to stand out in the workplace. Our General Body Meetings include interactive workshops, team-building activities, and guest speakers designed to prepare you for internships, jobs, and life after college. Workshops may cover résumé building, cover letters, interviews, networking, and how to stand out to recruiters. We also incorporate team-based activities, such as “What Would You Do?” business scenarios, where members work together to solve real-world workplace challenges and strengthen their communication, leadership, and decision-making skills. Guest speakers will include professionals from a variety of industries and career paths. Each meeting is an opportunity to learn a new skill, discover a profession you may not have considered, expand your network, and ask professionals the questions you have always wanted answered. Whether you are just beginning your professional journey or preparing to land your next internship or job, SHRM General Body Meetings are designed to help you become a more confident and prepared business professional.

events.title: Calming the Storm: Utilizing CALM for Early Childhood Anxiety
events.description: Date: Thursday, October 1st & Friday, October 2nd, 2026 Time: 9 a.m. - 1 p.m. ET (each day) Format: Live virtual training (link and access details will be provided upon registration) Cost: $250 for professionals / $50 for students Register here: https://redcap.fiu.edu/surveys/?s=DJHLHK7W8XWJNNF7 About the Talk: Enhance your clinical toolkit for treating early childhood anxiety through this dynamic, interactive workshop on one of the adaptations of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT). Focusing on the Coaching Approach behavior and Leading by Modeling (CALM) model, the workshop integrates didactic instruction, live demonstrations, video examples, role plays, and interactive activities to build a strong foundation in PCIT skills for anxiety. Participants will learn PRIDE skills, along with exposure-based strategies and parent coaching techniques to actively engage caregivers and support the generalization of gains beyond the therapy setting. Attendees will leave with a practical, hands-on toolkit to help caregivers shift from “rescuing” to “empowering” their child, transforming the parent-child relationship into a powerful driver of brave, flexible behavior. This presentation targets psychologists, clinicians, trainees, and students, offering content at a beginner/intermediate level. The speakers have reported no conflicts of interest or commercial support for this talk. Learning Objectives: 1.Describe multiple etiologies and trajectory for early childhood anxiety. 2.Identify 3 behavioral strategies (e.g., positive reinforcement, parent coaching, exposure) used in treating anxiety in young children. 3.Define the Child-Directed Interaction (CDI) skills and DADS skills necessary in PCIT-CALMfor early childhood anxiety. 4.Use the adapted PCIT methods in their clinical practice with youth with anxiety for greater overall care. About the Speakers: Dr. Jami Furr is a Clinical Associate Professor and Senior Psychologist in the Mental Health Interventions and Novel Therapeutics (MINT) Program, and Developer of the Selective Mutism Program at the Center for Children and Families (CCF) at Florida International University. Dr. Furr has extensive expertise in cognitive-behavioral treatments of childhood anxiety, trauma, and disruptive behavior disorders, with a particular focus on preschool mental health and children with selective mutism. She served as the Clinical Director and Supervisor for several federally and foundation-funded trials on adaptations of Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT), including the Internet-delivered Coaching Approach behavior and Learning by Modeling (CALM) program for young children with anxiety and the intensive group behavioral treatment for selective mutism (IGBT-SM). Dr. Furr also directed one of the first long-term outcome studies on youth with SM. She is the Past-President of the Selective Mutism Association and has continued to serve on their Board of Directors for the last 9 years. Dr. Furr currently provides training and supervision of graduate students conducting clinical services for anxiety, selective mutism, OCD, and/or disruptive behavior problems in youth. Carolina Costa is a Licensed Mental Health Counselor and Clinic Coordinator in the MINT Program at the Center for Children and Families (CCF) at Florida International University. Carolina has extensive clinical experience providing cognitive-behavioral treatment for childhood anxiety, with a particular focus on children and adolescents with selective mutism. She is bilingual in English and Spanish and provides clinical services in both languages. Carolina has experience providing individual and group-based interventions, as well as intensive services for children and adolescents. Her clinical experience also includes collaborating with teachers and school personnel through teacher consultation and providing in-classroom interventions to support children in applying treatment skills across school and other real-world settings. She additionally assists with the training and supervision of graduate students providing clinical services for anxiety, selective mutism, OCD, and disruptive behavior problems in youth. Carolina has served as the coordinator for clinical research studies, including the Kids Face-to-face And Computer-Enhanced Formats Effectiveness study for Anxiety and Related Symptoms (Kids FACE FEARS) and the Selective Mutism Intervention Long-term Evaluation (SMILE).

events.title: G20 Miami 2026 Preview: Innovation, Trade, and Collaboration
events.description: As America celebrates its 250th anniversary, Miami is proud to serve as the host region for the 2026 G20 in Doral, Florida this December. This global event will convene political and financial leaders from over 30 of the world’s major advanced and emerging economies to discuss and coordinate economic policy relating to areas such as innovation, trade, and energy. FIU and its partners invite you to a fun, dynamic preview event for G20 Miami 2026 here in the nation’s capital. Learn from US Government officials and G20 country representatives on what to expect this December in Miami. With a bent towards Innovation and tech, our experts will also relay what the outcomes of recent ministerial meetings mean for collaboration around AI and emerging technologies.

events.title: Women, Violence and Memory: The Human Legacy of the Partition of British India
events.description: The 1947 Partition of British India triggered one of the largest forced migrations in modern history, uprooting millions and transforming communities across the subcontinent. Women experienced this upheaval in profoundly gendered ways, facing abduction, sexual violence, displacement and the loss of family and home. This conversation explores women’s experiences of Partition and the memories carried across generations, examining how recovering often-silenced histories can deepen our understanding of violence, survival, displacement and the enduring human consequences of Partition. This event is presented as part of the programming for the exhibition Project Dastaan, currently on view in the Green School Gallery (SIPA I, Room 110).

events.title: TTR: Disaster Preparedness & Humanitarian Response
events.description: Tuesday Times Roundtable TTR is FIU’s weekly series of moderated conversations around current global issues and trends. Conversations bring into play the multiple viewpoints of students, faculty, staff, and community members. All sessions are absolutely FREE and lunch is on us! TTR: Disaster Preparedness & Humanitarian Response Presenter: Dulce Suarez, PhD, Assistant Director & Adjunct Professor, Academy for International Disaster Preparedness, FIU SDG Topic Category: SDG11: Sustainable Cities and Communities News Article: https://go.fiu.edu/ttr1006 Description: The discussion on Disaster Preparedness & Humanitarian Response will draw on Dr. Dulce M. Suarez’s experience in emergency management, higher education, and humanitarian operations. The presentation will explore the four phases of disaster management—mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery and examine how communities, institutions, and response organizations can strengthen readiness, improve coordination, and support effective humanitarian action before, during, and after disasters. Dr. Suarez will highlight lessons learned from real-world disaster response and recovery efforts, with particular attention to resilience, collaboration, and the value of strong partnerships across the public, private, nonprofit, and academic sectors. The discussion will also focus on how the State of Florida continues to strengthen emergency preparedness through training, exercises, and partnerships with universities such as Florida International University. These collaborations play an important role in developing the knowledge, practical skills, and leadership capabilities of the next generation of emergency management professionals. events.title: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ
events.description: La Hora del Café is a weekly conversation and community-building event hosted by the Department of Modern Languages at Florida International University (FIU). The event provides students, faculty, and language enthusiasts with an informal and welcoming environment to practice Spanish, strengthen intercultural communication skills, and connect with members of the FIU community. Held every Tuesday from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Department of Modern Languages (SIPA II, Room 216), La Hora del Café encourages participants of all proficiency levels to engage in spontaneous conversations in Spanish while enjoying complimentary coffee and pastries sponsored by Café Bustelo. The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty.

The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty. events.title: Period Talks: Real Talk, Real Cost
events.description: The Women’s Center will facilitate a discussion addressing pink tax and its impact on affordability and access to quality products and services. The pink tax refers to the higher prices often charged for products and services marketed towards women compared to similar items aimed at men. This phenomenon is not a formal tax but rather a pricing disparity observed in various consumer goods, including toiletries, clothing, and even personal services. For instance, studies have shown that items like women's razors and shampoos can be more expensive than their male counterparts, despite being nearly identical in function. The term "pink tax" is derived from the association of the color pink with femininity, leading to the notion that products tailored for women often carry a premium. The conversation will focus on understanding pink tax, period equity, and women’s reproductive health given current legislation. Need an accommodation or accessible materials? Contact the Office of Universal Access and Digital Compliance at accommodations@fiu.edu or 305-348-1576.

events.description: Join SHRM and build the confidence, skills, and professional presence you need to stand out in the workplace. Our General Body Meetings include interactive workshops, team-building activities, and guest speakers designed to prepare you for internships, jobs, and life after college. Workshops may cover résumé building, cover letters, interviews, networking, and how to stand out to recruiters. We also use “What Would You Do?” scenarios to help members practice solving real workplace challenges as a team. Guest speakers will include professionals from a variety of industries and career paths. Each meeting is an opportunity to learn a new skill, discover a profession you may not have considered, expand your network, and ask professionals the questions you have always wanted answered. Whether you are just beginning your professional journey or preparing to land your next internship or job, SHRM General Body Meetings are designed to help you become a more confident and prepared business professional. This Event is Open to all Students and Funded by SGA

events.title: The Stories We Carry: Project Dastaan and the Memory of Partition
events.description: Project Dastaan is an award-winning peacebuilding initiative that uses oral histories, animation and virtual reality to preserve the personal stories of those who experienced the 1947 Partition of British India and reconnect survivors with places left behind. By centering the experiences of those whose lives were transformed by displacement, the initiative explores how storytelling can bridge borders, generations and communities. Join us for a compelling conversation with Project Dastaan co-founders, award-winning filmmaker Sparsh Ahuja and journalist and artist Saadia Gardezi, as they discuss the origins of the project, the power of immersive storytelling and their efforts to transform memories of loss and separation into opportunities for dialogue, empathy and reconciliation. This event is presented as part of the programming for the exhibition Project Dastaan, currently on view in the Green School Gallery (SIPA I, Room 110).

events.title: Beyond Adversities
events.description: Beyond Adversity, taking place on October 8, is an inspiring conversation featuring Jorge Font and Ricardo Paván that explores resilience, disability inclusion, and the transformative power of sport. Through their personal experiences and leadership in adaptive sports and advocacy, Font and Paván will share how adversity can become a catalyst for growth, purpose, and meaningful impact. The event will challenge conventional perceptions of disability and ability while highlighting the importance of accessibility, equal opportunity, and inclusive communities. Beyond simply inspiring audiences to overcome personal challenges, Beyond Adversity seeks to encourage the FIU community to recognize inclusion as a shared responsibility and to redefine what is possible when barriers—physical, social, and cultural—are challenged. Founded by SGA; open to all students.

events.title: Bringing Skills into Action: Rethinking Engagement and Treatment Delivery for Youth and Adolescents with ADHD
events.description: About the speaker: Melissa R. Dvorsky, Ph.D., is a psychologist and Associate Professor at Children’s National Hospital and the George Washington University School of Medicine where she directs the ADHD & Learning Differences Program. She has authored over 70 peer-reviewed publications on ADHD with research funded by the National Institute of Mental Health and the U.S. Department of Education Institute of Education Sciences. Dr. Dvorsky developed the Advanced Tools for Organization Management (ATOM), a technology-enhanced organizational skills intervention for adolescents with ADHD. She is an Associate Editor of the Journal of Attention Disorders and serves on the editorial boards for the Journal of Youth & Adolescence and School Mental Health. Dr. Dvorsky’s research is focused on partnering with communities including schools and care providers, to improve the access, effectiveness, and sustainability of services for the ADHD community. About the talk: Evidence-based interventions for adolescents with ADHD can effectively target organizational, time-management, and related functional skills, yet treatment outcomes depend on adolescents’ engagement and ability to use these strategies in everyday contexts. This presentation will examine treatment engagement and skill utilization in adolescent ADHD, drawing on findings from a systematic review of cognitive-behavioral interventions that identifies common approaches for promoting engagement, research examining predictors of treatment engagement and differential treatment effects, and a school-based intervention augmented with novel mobile technology designed to support real-time skill use. Together, these findings illustrate opportunities to move beyond traditional approaches to intervention delivery by intentionally designing interventions to promote engagement, reinforce skill use, and provide support when and where adolescents need it. The presentation will highlight how engagement-focused strategies may enhance treatment response and will discuss implications for optimizing the delivery of ADHD interventions across school and outpatient settings. This presentation is relevant to mental health professionals, psychologists, clinicians, students, and trainees at an intermediate level. The speaker has reported no conflicts of interest or commercial support for this talk. Learning Objectives: Describe key components and common elements of cognitive-behavioral interventions for youth with ADHD.Evaluate the potential utility of digital tools for promoting real-time skill utilization and treatment engagement among adolescents with ADHD.At the conclusion of this presentation, participants will be able to: Analyze approaches for treatment engagement and factors associated with skill utilization among youth with ADHD.Apply research findings on treatment engagement and digital augmentation to identify opportunities for improving the delivery and effectiveness of ADHD interventions in clinical and school-based settings.Continuing Education: One hour of CE credit is available for attendees who are present for the entire program. We ask that all participants complete the given evaluation form at the conclusion of the program. The Center for Children and Families at FIU is approved by the American Psychological Association to sponsor continuing education for psychologists. The Center for Children and Families at FIU maintains responsibility for this program and its content. This free in-person talk has also been approved for up to 1 CEU credit by Florida Board of Clinical Social Work, Marriage and Family Therapy and Mental Health Counseling; and 1 CE credit by Florida Board of Psychology and Florida Office of School Psychology. Provider # BAP 50-12872. This event is proudly co-sponsored by the Department of Psychology.

events.title: Parents Growing Together Support Group
events.description: Parenting can be deeply rewarding—and at times, challenging and overwhelming. You don’t have to navigate it alone. Join us for a virtual Parent Support Group, a welcoming space to be heard, supported, and connected with other parents who understand the joys and complexities of raising children. Together, we will draw upon our own strengths, learn from one another’s experiences, and cultivate a more mindful approach to parenting—creating opportunities for connection, growth, healing, and resilience within ourselves, our families, and our community. The group is facilitated by a professional clinician and educator. Sessions begin on 9/11. Come as you are. Share, listen, connect, and grow. The group meets the 2nd Friday of every month via Zoom.

events.description: Join us for a Cybersecurity AI Hackathon & Career Upskilling Event, hosted in collaboration with ISACA South Florida Chapter, ITRADE STEM, and SIM South Florida. This hands-on event brings students and emerging tech talent together with cybersecurity and technology professionals to learn, build, and network. Teams will work alongside industry mentors to create a real-world solution using AI, cybersecurity, and automation. After a focused 3–4 hour challenge, teams will present their projects to a panel of industry judges, with prizes awarded for 1st, 2nd, and 3rd place. Whether you're looking to build your skills, gain hands-on experience, meet industry professionals, or break into cybersecurity, this event is designed to connect South Florida's next generation of cyber talent with today's industry leaders.

events.title: Sacred Sound and Movement
events.description: Ecstatic dance is the art of free movement—an invitation to surrender to rhythm and let music guide you inward. Much like meditation, it can open the door to altered states of awareness. Across cultures and traditions, dance has long been celebrated as a path to serenity, insight and connection with the divine. Many describe a profound sense of unity—with others, with the Earth and with their own inner being. Our journey begins by awakening life force through guided breathwork and visualization, gently preparing body and mind. From there, we flow into a spirited dance session led by a live DJ, allowing movement to carry us into expansion and joy. We then settle into stillness, immersed in the resonance of gong, quartz crystal bowls and ancient sound-healing instruments. This soundscape creates space for deep restoration, drawing on the timeless art of sound healing—where vibration itself becomes medicine, restoring balance throughout the body. Join us for this interactive experience exploring the transformative power of sacred sound and movement. As a special gift, each participant will receive a crystal gemstone to take home—a lasting reminder of the journey. Please bring a yoga mat and water bottle.

events.title: Writers on the Bay: Stacey Waite
events.description: The Writers on the Bay Reading Series presents Stacey Waite Stacey Waite is the Susan J. Rosowski Associate Professor of English at the University of Nebraska - Lincoln and is the author of five collections of poetry: Choke (winner of the Frank O’Hara Prize for Poetry), Love Poem to Androgyny, the lake has no saint (Winner of the Snowbound Prize for Poetry), Butch Geography (2013), and A Real Man Would Have A Gun (University of New Mexico Press, 2025). Waite is also the author of Teaching Queer: Radical Possibilities for Writing and Knowing (University of Pittsburgh Press, 2017). Working in both creative writing and composition studies, Waite is also co-editor of Inventing the Discipline: Student Work in Composition Studies and the textbook, Ways of Reading. Waite’s poetry and essays have appeared in such journals as Writing on the Edge, Assay, New Territory, Literacy in Composition Studies, and Black Warrior Review. Waite’s poems have been anthologized in a range of collections including Best American Poetry and The Norton Introduction to Literature. Waite's most recent collection was shortlisted for the Lambda Literary Award in LGBTQ+ Poetry. Visit Waite’s website at www.staceywaite.com.

events.title: José López: Schubert, Liszt & the Romantic Piano
events.description: Pianist José López, Professor and Coordinator of the Piano Program at FIU, brings together four distinctive voices of the Romantic era in a program of rich contrasts. Schubert’s Sonata in A minor, D. 537, and selections from Liszt’s late piano works are presented alongside music by Charles-Valentin Alkan and Ferdinand Hiller’s Piano Sonata No. 2 in A-flat major, Op. 59. The program pairs celebrated composers with less familiar works, offering audiences a fresh perspective on the nineteenth-century piano repertoire. The program features Franz Schubert's Sonata in A minor (D. 537), a work by C.V. Alkan, Liszt's late piano works, and Ferdinand Hiller's Sonata Op. 59.

events.title: FIU Dundas Studio Recital - Mélodies d’Automne
events.description: Step into the golden glow of autumn through the enchanting world of French art song. Featuring selections by Fauré, Debussy, Duparc, Chausson, Hahn, Poulenc, and others, this intimate recital weaves together poetry, passion, nostalgia, and dreamlike beauty. From shimmering twilight landscapes to tender reflections on love and memory, Mélodies d’Automne celebrates the season's rich colors and quiet magic through some of France’s most beloved “melodies.” Join us for an afternoon of elegance, warmth, and musical storytelling, presented by singers from the voice studio of Prof. Robert B. Dundas and accompanied by pianist Masami Miyazaki.

events.title: SGA Fly-In
events.description: The SGA Executive Team will participate in FIU’s DC Fly-In, a three-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at how policies are made and the career opportunities available in Washington, D.C. events.title: Beyond the Academic Paper: Writing Op-Eds For Policy Impact on Latin America
events.description: One of the most important components of an interdiscplinary education is learning how to conduct research and prepare academic papers. However, for those interested in working in policy, one of the most important skills that they can learn is how to distill the complex information learned through research into a condensed format that is more likely to be read by both policymakers and the general public— particularly through op-eds. This is particularly true for those that seek to influence policy—whether locally, nationally, or even globally—through their research. Navigating the op-ed writing and pitch process can, however, be daunting. This Op-Ed Writing Workshop will lay out the purpose and fundamentals of op-ed writing for policy audiences. Main topics or areas that will be covered: Writing for policy audiences, role for op-eds in the policy process, translating research and analysis into policy-relevant and impactful op-eds. Expected outcomes or skills participants will gain: Participants will learn how public writing can impact the policy-making process and the fundamentals of op-ed writing, pitching, and disseminating. Workshop Facilitator: Adam Ratzlaff, founder and CEO of Pan-American Strategic Advisors—a next-generation think tank and consulting firm focused on the Western Hemisphere—and a member of The Expert Network (TEN) with Diplomatic Courier's World in 2050. He has authored or co-authored over 150 public-facing and academic works on regional affairs, and his op-eds have been featured across local, national, and international outlets including Foreign Policy, The National Interest, LatinoAmerica21, Latinometrics, and Responsible Statecraft.

events.title: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ
events.description: La Hora del Café is a weekly conversation and community-building event hosted by the Department of Modern Languages at Florida International University (FIU). The event provides students, faculty, and language enthusiasts with an informal and welcoming environment to practice Spanish, strengthen intercultural communication skills, and connect with members of the FIU community. Held every Tuesday from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Department of Modern Languages (SIPA II, Room 216), La Hora del Café encourages participants of all proficiency levels to engage in spontaneous conversations in Spanish while enjoying complimentary coffee and pastries sponsored by Café Bustelo. The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty.

events.title: Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting & Exposition
events.description: The Association of the United States Army (AUSA) Annual Meeting & Exposition is the premier land power exposition and professional development forum in North America—and the must-attend event for anyone involved in the defense sector. With over 44,000 attendees, 750+ exhibits, and representation from 92 countries, this three-day event is where the global defense community converges to shape the future of national security. Held in the heart of the nation’s capital, the AUSA Annual Meeting is more than just a trade show—it’s a strategic platform that connects military leaders, industry innovators, policymakers, and international delegations. Attendees gain exclusive insights into U.S. Army priorities, explore cutting-edge technologies, and engage in high-impact networking with key decision-makers.

events.title: NSE Food Drive
events.description: From October 14th to October 30th, we are coming together to support our fellow Panthers in need! The National Student Exchange Club is hosting a food drive to benefit the FIU Food Pantry, and we need your help to make a difference. Bring non-perishable food items to GC 341, and let's show our Panther pride by supporting our community. Every contribution counts and will go a long way in providing essential resources to those facing food insecurity. Every item makes an impact. Let's unite as a community and demonstrate the true spirit of generosity. Together, we can help our fellow students thrive! Recommended donations Non-perishable food items and toiletries. The items include but are not limited to: Dairy: canned and boxed milk, evaporated milk and powder milk Protein: Canned meats, peanut/nut butter, canned or dried beans Fruit: canned fruit, dry fruit, fruit cups Grains: Boxed pasta, rice and rice mixes, cereal, oatmeal, and mac and cheese. Misc: pasta sauce, condiments and snacks.

events.title: SGA Fly-In
events.description: The SGA Executive Team will participate in FIU’s DC Fly-In, a three-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at how policies are made and the career opportunities available in Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, academia, and industry through conversations, experiences, and opportunities to explore issues that matter to them. The Fly-In also provides an opportunity to draft policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, giving the SGA Executive Team a firsthand experience with the policy process and the opportunity to connect their student leadership experience to issues affecting FIU students.

events.title: Using the FRS to Plan for Your Retirement
events.description: This 90-minute retirement planning workshop provides an overview of the FRS and helps you understand the nuts and bolts of planning for your retirement. The workshop will demonstrate how everyday living expenses and inflation dramatically reduce your fixed retirement income. You will see the role the FRS Retirement Plans play in meeting your financial goals as well as the income gap that must be made up through saving and investing. You will leave the workshop with a full understanding of the ongoing financial planning resources available to you as a member of the FRS.

events.title: The Unseen Made Visible: Rafał Olbiński on Art, Imagination and Freedom of Expression
events.description: Step into the imaginative world of acclaimed Polish-American artist Rafał Olbiński, whose dreamlike images transform the familiar into the unexpected. In this engaging conversation, Olbiński reflects on surrealism, symbolism and the creative process, exploring the power of art to challenge convention, reveal hidden truths and expand the boundaries of what we see and understand. Drawing on a remarkable international career, he considers the essential role of imagination and freedom of expression in art, culture and contemporary society.

events.title: SHRM General Body Meeting
events.description: Join SHRM and build the confidence, skills, and professional presence you need to stand out in the workplace. Our General Body Meetings include interactive workshops, team-building activities, and guest speakers designed to prepare you for internships, jobs, and life after college. Workshops may cover résumé building, cover letters, interviews, networking, and how to stand out to recruiters. We also use “What Would You Do?” scenarios to help members practice solving real workplace challenges as a team. Guest speakers will include professionals from a variety of industries and career paths. Each meeting is an opportunity to learn a new skill, discover a profession you may not have considered, expand your network, and ask professionals the questions you have always wanted answered. Whether you are just beginning your professional journey or preparing to land your next internship or job, SHRM General Body Meetings are designed to help you become a more confident and prepared business professional. This Event is Open to all Students and Funded by SGA

events.title: College of Business Master in Cybersecurity Fly-In
events.description: The College of Business Master in Cybersecurity DC Fly-In is a two-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at the intersection of cybersecurity, technology, policy, and national security in Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, industry, academia, and the broader cybersecurity community to explore how policy is developed and how cybersecurity professionals are shaping the future. The Fly-In will provide opportunities to learn about cybersecurity careers in the nation’s capital, engage in conversations with leaders working across the field, and gain a deeper understanding of the policies and challenges influencing the cybersecurity landscape. Students will also have the opportunity to explore policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, connecting their academic experience to real-world issues and opportunities in Washington, D.C.

events.title: Sound of the Soul: An Introduction to the Bhagavad Gita
events.description: Dr. Graham Schweig, a longtime scholar of comparative religion, offers a clear and welcoming introduction to the Bhagavad Gita, one of India’s great spiritual and philosophical texts. Set on the eve of a great battle, the Gita explores timeless questions of duty, action and the nature of the self. Its teachings have resonated with generations of readers around the world, including figures as diverse as Albert Einstein, Steve Jobs and Tupac Shakur. This talk is designed for students encountering the Gita for the first time, as well as those who already know it and want to go deeper. Join us for an accessible introduction to a text that has shaped global philosophy and spirituality for millennia.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival Opening Night: Amernet Performs Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 + Mendelssohn’s Octet
events.description: The 2026 FIU Music Festival opens with an extraordinary anniversary performance celebrating 30 years of the Wertheim Performing Arts Center and the Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts. The Amernet String Quartet, FIU’s Artist-in-Residence ensemble, anchors an evening of masterworks, opening with Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto No. 3 and continuing with Mendelssohn’s Octet, performed alongside Wertheim alumni and current students. Bach’s Brandenburg Concerto is brilliant, precise, and full of motion—an intricate conversation among instruments that still feels alive more than 300 years later. Mendelssohn’s Octet answers with youthful fire: sweeping, urgent, and astonishingly assured for a composer just sixteen years old. This milestone concert celebrates the full reach of Wertheim’s musical community: students beginning their professional journeys, alumni returning with the depth of experience, and faculty mentors whose leadership continues to shape the next generation. On one stage, past, present, and future come together in a powerful reflection of what the Wertheim has built over three decades. More than a festival opening, this performance is a celebration of excellence, mentorship, and community—a portrait of a living institution where talent is developed, relationships endure, and music continues to connect generations of musicians and audiences.

events.title: College of Business Master in Cybersecurity Fly-In
events.description: The College of Business Master in Cybersecurity DC Fly-In is a two-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at the intersection of cybersecurity, technology, policy, and national security in Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, industry, academia, and the broader cybersecurity community to explore how policy is developed and how cybersecurity professionals are shaping the future. The Fly-In will provide opportunities to learn about cybersecurity careers in the nation’s capital, engage in conversations with leaders working across the field, and gain a deeper understanding of the policies and challenges influencing the cybersecurity landscape. Students will also have the opportunity to explore policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, connecting their academic experience to real-world issues and opportunities in Washington, D.C.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: FIU Jazz All-Stars: A Wertheim Homecoming
events.description: In celebration of the 30th anniversary of the Herbert and Nicole Wertheim School of Music & Performing Arts, six of the School’s accomplished jazz alumni return for a special performance with the FIU Studio Jazz Band. Trumpeter Jean Caze, guitarist Aaron Lebos, pianist Kemuel Roig, bassist Kai Sanchez, saxophonist Dave Fernandez, and drummer Rodolfo Zuniga have established wide-ranging careers as performers, composers, bandleaders, recording artists, and educators. Collectively, their credits span more than 30 albums and recording projects as leaders and co-leaders, along with dozens of additional recordings—including Grammy- and Latin Grammy-winning projects. Their achievements include major national and international jazz competition honors, acclaimed releases, and appearances at prominent venues and festivals around the world. They have performed or recorded with celebrated artists including Herbie Hancock, Aretha Franklin, Gloria Estefan, Arturo Sandoval, Julio Iglesias, Paquito D’Rivera, Randy Brecker, and many others.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Arias and American Voices
events.description: Acclaimed soprano and FIU alumna Laura León returns to the FIU Music Festival with internationally renowned pianist Robert Koenig for Arias to American Voices, a program that moves from the operatic stage to the breadth of American song. Opening with arias that showcase León’s coloratura, dramatic presence, and exceptional range, the evening then turns to a commemoration of America’s 250th anniversary. Works by George Gershwin, Leonard Bernstein, Douglas Moore, Margaret Bonds, and others bring together American opera, Broadway, spirituals, and folk traditions. León earned critical acclaim as the Queen of the Night in Mozart’s The Magic Flute and has undertaken the demanding roles of all four heroines in Offenbach’s The Tales of Hoffmann. Koenig, a graduate of the Curtis Institute of Music, has performed at Carnegie Hall, the Kennedy Center, Amsterdam’s Concertgebouw, the Louvre, and other major venues around the world. Presented in partnership with Friends of Chamber Music of Miami.

events.description: Registration is now LIVE for Aspen Conexión’s 6th Annual Advancing Economic Mobility Summit on October 18–19, 2026 in Miami, Florida! As a strategic gateway to Latin America and Spain and one of the most dynamic cities in the U.S. today, Miami provides an ideal setting for this year’s Summit. events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Toomai String Quintet
events.description: Concert | 5:00 p.m. The FIU Music Festival welcomes the Toomai String Quintet for a program bringing together music, dance and the screen—including a suite from Carlos Rafael Rivera’s Grammy-winning score for the Netflix series The Queen’s Gambit. Formed at The Juilliard School, Toomai is known for crossing musical traditions and expanding the repertoire for string ensemble. Its commitment to Latin American music has led to more than 30 arrangements and commissions and two acclaimed recordings, Cuerdas Cubanas and Passos Brasileiros. The program places music by Pulitzer Prize-winning composer Tania León and Cuban composer and guitarist Leo Brouwer alongside works by three composers with deep ties to FIU: Distinguished University Professor Orlando Jacinto García and alumni Carlos Rafael Rivera ’96 and Marcus Norris ’17. Rivera’s Queen’s Gambit Suite draws from the score that earned him both Grammy and Emmy awards. A member of the School of Music’s first graduating class in 1996, Rivera has built an acclaimed career in film and television. Norris’s work spans concert music, opera, film and television, often bringing classical music into conversation with hip-hop, R&B and other contemporary traditions. The concert’s theatrical centerpiece is García’s prohibido (prohibited). Premiered at the New World Center in January 2025 by the New World Symphony with dancers from Miami City Ballet, the work returns in an intimate version for Toomai. Dancers Emily Bromberg and Alexander Sokolov of Dimensions Dance Theatre of Miami perform Ariel Rose’s choreography, with video by Jacek Kolasinski and John Stuart. Combining music, dance, video and spoken text in English and Spanish, prohibido confronts repression based on race, religion, beliefs, sexual orientation and other aspects of identity. The work reimagines García’s earlier string quartet I Never Saw Another Butterfly, written in memory of the children imprisoned at Terezín. Preconcert Conversation | 4:30 p.m. FIU alumni Carlos Rafael Rivera ’96 and Marcus Norris ’17 return to FIU for a special conversation with Orlando Jacinto García about their music, their connections to the university and careers spanning the concert hall, opera, film and television. Concert Program Tania León: Tumbao Marcus Norris: My Idols Are Dead Leo Brouwer: Música incidental campesina Carlos Rafael Rivera: Queen’s Gambit Suite Orlando Jacinto García: prohibido (prohibited) Featuring dancers Emily Bromberg and Alexander Sokolov of Dimensions Dance Theatre of Miami Choreography by Ariel Rose Video by Jacek Kolasinski and John Stuart

events.title: Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In
events.description: The Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In is a three-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at how policy is developed and how global and public affairs shape Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, academia, think tanks, and industry through conversations and experiences focused on current international and public policy issues. The Fly-In will provide opportunities to explore career pathways in the nation’s capital, connect classroom learning to real-world policy challenges, and gain a deeper understanding of the people and institutions shaping public policy. Students will also have the opportunity to develop policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, bringing their academic interests and perspectives directly into the policy process.

events.title: Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In
events.description: The Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In is a three-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at how policy is developed and how global and public affairs shape Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, academia, think tanks, and industry through conversations and experiences focused on current international and public policy issues. The Fly-In will provide opportunities to explore career pathways in the nation’s capital, connect classroom learning to real-world policy challenges, and gain a deeper understanding of the people and institutions shaping public policy. Students will also have the opportunity to develop policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, bringing their academic interests and perspectives directly into the policy process.

events.title: Alumni Speaker Series: Beyond the Clinic: Leadership, Entrepreneurship, & the Future of Physical Therapy
events.description: Join the Nursing and Health Sciences Student Council for the inaugural Alumni Speaker Series, a new initiative designed to connect students with accomplished alumni who are making a lasting impact in their fields. Our featured speaker, Dr. Jose Martinez, a proud alumnus of the Nicole Wertheim College of Nursing & Health Sciences Physical Therapy program, is the Founder and CEO of Propel Physical Therapy. As an entrepreneur, healthcare leader, and clinician, Dr. Martinez has built a successful practice while helping shape the future of patient-centered care. During this engaging discussion, Dr. Martinez will share his professional journey from student to healthcare executive, offering valuable insights into leadership development, entrepreneurship, innovation in healthcare, and emerging trends within the physical therapy profession. Attendees will gain a deeper understanding of the opportunities and challenges facing the industry and learn how to position themselves for success in an evolving healthcare landscape. Whether you are interested in clinical practice, private practice ownership, healthcare leadership, or professional growth, this event offers a unique opportunity to learn from an accomplished alumnus, ask questions, and expand your professional network. events.title: From Evidence to Impact: Building a Tobacco-Free Future Through Workforce Development & Health System Transformation with Babalola Faseru, MBChB, MPH
events.description: Babalola Faseru, MBChB, MPH, is a professor of population and community health at the University of Kansas Medical Center and a consultant medical epidemiologist with the Kansas Department of Health and Environment. An internationally recognized tobacco control researcher, Faseru focuses on integrating evidence-based tobacco treatment into health care systems and community settings. He directs the Kansas Tobacco Treatment Specialist Training Program and leads initiatives that expand smoking cessation capacity among public health, health care and school professionals. A fellow of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco, Faseru has authored numerous peer-reviewed publications and contributes to national and global efforts to advance tobacco dependence treatment and population health. REGISTER HERE Lunch will be provided. This event is part of the Dr. Herbert and Nicole Wertheim Leadership Lecture Series.

events.description: Tuesday Times Roundtable TTR is FIU’s weekly series of moderated conversations around current global issues and trends. Conversations bring into play the multiple viewpoints of students, faculty, staff, and community members. All sessions are absolutely FREE and lunch is on us! TTR: From Awareness to Action: Empowering Change Through Community Engagement Presenter: Bill Bigelow, Program Manager, Clean Miami Beach SDG Topic Category: SDG12: Responsible Consumption & Production News Article: fiu.edu/ttr1020 Description: This session will explore how community engagement and environmental action can contribute to the protection and long-term health of Biscayne Bay and South Florida’s coastal ecosystems. Participants will learn about Clean Miami Beach’s grassroots approach to addressing marine debris, plastic pollution, habitat degradation, and other environmental challenges through beach cleanups, education, and community outreach. The discussion will highlight how science-based initiatives can empower students, residents, and local partners to become active environmental stewards. Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of the connection between local environmental challenges and broader sustainability goals, as well as practical ways to turn environmental awareness into meaningful community action. events.title: LA HORA DEL CAFÉ
events.description: La Hora del Café is a weekly conversation and community-building event hosted by the Department of Modern Languages at Florida International University (FIU). The event provides students, faculty, and language enthusiasts with an informal and welcoming environment to practice Spanish, strengthen intercultural communication skills, and connect with members of the FIU community. Held every Tuesday from 3:00 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. in the Department of Modern Languages (SIPA II, Room 216), La Hora del Café encourages participants of all proficiency levels to engage in spontaneous conversations in Spanish while enjoying complimentary coffee and pastries sponsored by Café Bustelo. The initiative supports the department's mission of promoting language learning beyond the classroom by creating authentic opportunities for oral communication, cultural exchange, and community engagement. Through relaxed conversation and peer interaction, participants develop confidence in their Spanish-speaking abilities, expand their cultural awareness, and build meaningful connections with fellow students and faculty.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Vincent Dubois, organ (Notre-Dame de Paris) and Marie-Andrée Joerger, accordion
events.description: A rare musical encounter comes to Miami when Vincent Dubois, titular organist of Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, and internationally acclaimed accordion virtuoso Marie-Andrée Joerger bring their organ-and-accordion duo to FIU for their first official U.S. tour together. Performed on the Sydell Ida Wertheim Concert Organ, this FIU Music Festival program reimagines music of sweeping color, elegance and dance through an unexpected pairing of instruments capable of both grandeur and intimacy. The evening opens with Khachaturian’s brilliant Masquerade Waltz before moving through the refined French sound world of Debussy’s Petite Suite, Fauré’s Dolly Suite and Poulenc’s Suite française. Bartók’s Romanian Folk Dances adds earthy rhythm and folk-inspired vitality, leading into the modern pulse of Patrice Caratini’s La valse des crayons. For Miami audiences, the program’s tango-infused finale offers a special charge: Richard Galliano’s Tango pour Claude and Piazzolla’s Invierno Porteño and La Muerte del Ángel bring the evening to a close with music of elegance, tension and unmistakable dramatic force. Inventive, virtuosic and deeply atmospheric, this concert reveals the organ and accordion in thrilling conversation—expanding familiar repertoire into something fresh, vivid and entirely unexpected.

events.title: Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In
events.description: The Steven J. Green School of International & Public Affairs Fly-In is a three-day experiential seminar designed to give students a firsthand look at how policy is developed and how global and public affairs shape Washington, D.C. Students will engage with experts across government, academia, think tanks, and industry through conversations and experiences focused on current international and public policy issues. The Fly-In will provide opportunities to explore career pathways in the nation’s capital, connect classroom learning to real-world policy challenges, and gain a deeper understanding of the people and institutions shaping public policy. Students will also have the opportunity to develop policy solutions and participate in advocacy meetings on Capitol Hill, bringing their academic interests and perspectives directly into the policy process.

events.title: SHRM General Body Meeting
events.description: Join SHRM and build the confidence, skills, and professional presence you need to stand out in the workplace. Our General Body Meetings include interactive workshops, team-building activities, and guest speakers designed to prepare you for internships, jobs, and life after college. Workshops may cover résumé building, cover letters, interviews, networking, and how to stand out to recruiters. We also incorporate team-based activities, such as “What Would You Do?” business scenarios, where members work together to solve real-world workplace challenges and strengthen their communication, leadership, and decision-making skills. Guest speakers will include professionals from a variety of industries and career paths. Each meeting is an opportunity to learn a new skill, discover a profession you may not have considered, expand your network, and ask professionals the questions you have always wanted answered. Whether you are just beginning your professional journey or preparing to land your next internship or job, SHRM General Body Meetings are designed to help you become a more confident and prepared business professional.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Liszt & Jiménez: Piano, Song, and Virtuosity
events.description: Celebrate Franz Liszt’s birthday with pianists Kemal Gekić and José López and guest soprano Sonya Baker in a festival concert spanning solo piano, chamber music and song. The program pairs Liszt’s solo works with music by Afro-Cuban composer and virtuoso pianist José Manuel Jiménez (1852–1917). López presents Jiménez’s solo piano works and two chamber compositions, while Baker—who made her Carnegie Hall debut with conductor Michael Tilson Thomas—joins him for a selection of Lieder. FIU Artist-in-Residence and longtime Miami International Piano Festival artist Kemal Gekić brings his celebrated command of Liszt to the composer’s solo piano works. His performances and recordings have earned international acclaim, including the Rosette Award from The Penguin Guide to Classical Recordings for his recording of the Rossini-Liszt transcriptions. Presented in collaboration with the South Florida Chapter of the American Liszt Society, the concert places a towering figure of the Romantic era alongside a compelling Afro-Cuban voice deserving of wider recognition.

events.title: 2026 FIU Music Festival: Piano Fireworks: Weber’s Musical Legacy
events.description: Two internationally acclaimed pianists explore the brilliant musical imagination of Carl Maria von Weber in a festival concert of solo and duet music. Lindsay Garritson and Ukrainian-born pianist Anastasiya Naplekova come together in a program featuring works composed by Weber alongside music inspired by his enduring influence. Garritson has appeared at Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center and earned top honors at major international piano competitions. Naplekova, praised for her “effortless virtuosity,” is a laureate of the Olga Kern, Hilton Head, Paderewski and Horowitz international piano competitions. Moving between dazzling solo showcases and the excitement of two pianists performing together, the program reveals Weber’s gift for drama, lyricism and brilliant keyboard writing—and the music his legacy inspired across generations. Experience two formidable pianists in an exhilarating celebration of Weber and his musical legacy at The Wertheim, an All-Steinway School.

events.title: Honorlock Training
events.description: The Honorlock training will provide comprehensive guidance on integrating Honorlock with Canvas to secure exams. Instructors will learn how to activate the tool, enable its features for quizzes, and manage critical session emails. The training will cover Honorlock's key features like screen capturing, disabling copy/pasting, secondary device detection, and "Search and Destroy" functionality for test content. It will also delve into the advanced options available for recording and restrictions during assessments. Monitoring and reporting features for student assessments will be discussed, alongside best practices for instructors and technical requirements for students. events.title: The Treatment of Immigrants, Refugees and Exiles: A Psychiatrist's Reflections on a Forty Year Journey with Eugenio Rothe, M.D.
events.description: Dr. Rothe is a professor of psychiatry and a founding faculty member of the FIU Herbert Wertheim College of Medicine. He also serves as an adjunct professor at FIU’s Cuban Research Institute and the Latin American and Caribbean Center. A distinguished life fellow of both the American Psychiatric Association and the American Academy of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Psychoanalysis, Rothe has dedicated his career to advancing mental health care. His work has focused extensively on the mental health needs of immigrant populations, with particular attention to psychological trauma, and he has written widely on these topics. REGISTER HERE Lunch will be provided. This event is part of the Department of Cellular & Molecular Medicine Seminar Series.

events.title: TTR: The State of Global Democracy and Human Rights: How We Can Fight Back Through Advocacy
events.description: Tuesday Times Roundtable TTR is FIU’s weekly series of moderated conversations around current global issues and trends. Conversations bring into play the multiple viewpoints of students, faculty, staff, and community members. Register at go.fiu.edu/ttronline TTR: The State of Global Democracy and Human Rights: How We Can Fight Back Through Advocacy Presenters: Katie LaRoque, Director, Policy & Advocacy, Freedom HouseBrian Tronic, Director of Free Them All: The Fred Hiatt Program To Free Political Prisoners, Freedom HousePrachi Lalwani, Senior Development & Operations Specialist, Freedom HouseSDG Topic Category: SDG16: Peace, Justice, and Strong InstitutionsNews Article: https://go.fiu.edu/ttr1027 Description: This session will provide an overview of the current state of global democracy and human rights, highlighting key trends and challenges identified through Freedom House's Freedom in the World research. Participants will learn about Freedom House's mission and work advancing freedom and supporting democracy worldwide. The discussion will also explore how advocacy can be a powerful tool for change, featuring examples of efforts to defend human rights, support political prisoners, and mobilize action on behalf of individuals and communities facing repression. Attendees will leave with a deeper understanding of today's human rights landscape and practical ways to engage in advocacy that advances freedom and democratic values.Register at go.fiu.edu/ttronlineADA Accommodation: Need an accommodation or accessible materials? Contact the Office of Universal Access and Digital Compliance at accommodations@fiu.edu or 305-348-1576.
